subject: Azure private offer — SOW billing cadence & data residency addendum
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: procurement@acme.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 27 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Azure private offer — initial addendum and SOW billing cadence

Hi Juan / Acme procurement team,

Thanks again for the time last week. Attached is a first-pass addendum to the Azure Private Offer that captures the SOW billing cadence we discussed and an initial data residency clause for the customer-controlled keys. Highlights: 
- Monthly invoicing for reserved capacity with 30-day net payment terms (we can shift to 45 days for enterprise finance).
- SKU entitlement schedule attached (separate spreadsheet) with units, overage rates, and regional mapping.
- Data residency: primary tenancy in East US with EU-DR replica available in West Europe. We proposed cross-border processing language and a customer-managed KMS option.

Can you confirm the procurement team’s preferred payment cadence and whether Acme requires an IP/escrow clause for model weights before legal redlines?

Next steps: we’ll take your markups and push into our legal template, then submit a private offer update on the Azure Portal for your review.

Attachments: Redwood_Azure_Private_Addendum_v1.docx; SKU_Entitlement_Schedule.xlsx

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Manager, Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

--

From: Juan Santiago <j.santiago@acme.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 28 May 2025 14:35:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Azure private offer — initial addendum and SOW billing cadence

Jordan —

Thanks for the docs. Quick notes from Acme procurement (high level):

1) Payment cadence: Acme prefers quarterly invoicing aligned to milestone acceptance for SOWs. Net 45 is preferred. Monthly reserved-capacity billing is acceptable for the SKU charges if we can aggregate to quarterly for bookkeeping.
2) Data residency: we need explicit contractual guarantees for EU customer data to remain in EU geography. The KMS option is good but we will need a proof-of-compliance checklist (SOC2 + Azure region attestations).
3) IP/escrow: Finance flagged this as a potential blocker for our legal; they want to understand licensing bounds versus model redistribution. A short call with your legal team would help.

We’ll send a redline by Friday with line comments. In the meantime, please confirm if Redwood can accept net 45 and a quarterly invoice aggregate for the SOW.

Regards,
Juan Santiago
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Financial
procurement@acme.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: j.santiago@acme.com, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com, olga.petrov@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 30 May 2025 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Azure private offer — initial addendum and SOW billing cadence

Juan / team,

Appreciate the quick response — cc’ing our procurement lead (Aditya) and legal ops (Olga) to address the items you raised. A few clarifications from our side: 

• Net 45 — we can accept net 45 for SOW line items, and will configure the reserved capacity SKU billing to produce monthly invoices that Redwood will aggregate and issue quarterly to Acme if that helps with your internal cadence. We will call this out in the billing exhibit.

• Data residency & compliance evidence — Olga, can you prepare the SOC2 attestation + Azure region residency statement and a short compliance checklist (what we can commit to for the private offer) so we can attach it to the addendum?

• IP / model redistribution — short version: licensed runtime access for your tenants only; no transfer of model weights. We’re happy to have a 30-minute sync with your legal to walk through the licensing table.

Juan — if you can send the procurement redline, we’ll review and aim to have an internal marked-up addendum by Wednesday. After that, our legal will push the update into the Azure Private Offer and share the DocuSign link.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Strategic Procurement Partnerships
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0199

Attachments referenced: compliance-evidence-template.pdf (will share in next email)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: j.santiago@acme.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 03 June 2025 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Azure private offer — initial addendum and SOW billing cadence

Juan / Acme legal team,

Following up with the requested compliance material. Attached is a short compliance checklist and the SOC2 bridge letter plus region residency statement that map to the addendum clauses. I also attached the SKU entitlement workbook with an example quarterly aggregation calculation. Please note the following items that typically trigger legal comments: 

1) Data residency clause: our standard private-offer language allows for regional tenancy guarantees for customer data processed on dedicated capacity; however, cross-border incident response may require a joint process exception — we added an operational annex that defines notification timeframes.

2) Escrow / IP: Redwood’s standard position is to not escrow model weights; we offer a mutual inspection right under NDA and a runtime licensing schedule. If Acme insists on escrow, we will need to scope the exact deliverable and costs for maintenance.

3) Billing dispute resolution: we included a 60-day dispute window and an invoice reconciliation clause to allow Acme to request backup (logs and per-SKU usage export) for contested charges.

Next steps: I’ve included comments inline in Redwood_Azure_Private_Addendum_v1.docx and uploaded a DocuSign draft to the related link below. If Acme legal can review the checklist and confirm the escrow stance, we can finalize and create the private offer update in Azure.

Attachments: Redwood_Azure_Private_Addendum_v1.docx (redlines), SKU_Entitlement_Schedule.xlsx (updated), Compliance_Checklist_SOC2_EU.pdf

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Legal Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com
